revisions.body: Hippias’s reply is also a piece of self-presentation. He portrays himself as the man who publicly offers both prepared displays and answers to anyone who asks. That makes Socrates’ question a challenge to the role Hippias has just claimed: refusing it would sit badly with his public promise. I would not take this pledge as Socrates’ verdict on Achilles and Odysseus; it commits Hippias to the inquiry before it settles anything.
